grounded_facts: Rowan Davenport disarms the boy by grabbing his gun hand, firing into the air, and taking him hostage to demand information.
Rowan Davenport grabs the boy and demands to know where he is, using physical force.
memories.memory_text: I saw Rowan Davenport grab the boy's gun hand, wrench it hard until it fired into the air, then take control of the gun and choke the boy while demanding to know where he was.

grounded_facts: The girl points a shotgun at Rowan Davenport and demands he release the boy.
memories.memory_text: I pointed my shotgun at Rowan Davenport and shouted at him to let the boy go, ready to shoot if he didn't.

grounded_facts: Rowan Davenport uses the oil lantern to knock the girl down, retrieves the shotgun, and gains full control of both weapons.
memories.memory_text: I remember Rowan Davenport kicking the oil lantern at me, the burning oil spilling on my leg, making me drop the shotgun before he snatched it up after tossing the boy into me.

grounded_facts: Rowan Davenport discovers that both the handgun and shotgun are unloaded, revealing the kids' bluff.
memories.memory_text: I think Rowan Davenport must have realized our weapons were empty after he took them, since neither the handgun nor the shotgun had any rounds in them.

grounded_facts: Nico Nolan pulls Rowan Davenport to cover just in time to avoid detection by a passing Hunter-Killer vehicle.
memories.memory_text: I saw Nico Nolan pull Rowan Davenport to cover just as a Hunter-Killer passed by, yelling that they'd seen the light.

grounded_facts: A tense confrontation and exchange between Rowan Davenport and two teenage survivors at a highway off-ramp.
memories.memory_text: I remember the tense moment when I approached Rowan Davenport with Nico Nolan, questioning where he was going, and how things escalated when I saw him rummaging through debris—I had to frisk him, and when I found those paper scraps, I wasn't sure what to make of them. I kept my shotgun on him, ready to act, and when he suddenly threw Nico Nolan at me, we both went down. I scrambled to put out the fire on my clothes with snow, and later, when the H-K passed, I stayed close, still not trusting him.

grounded_facts: Nico Nolan tells Rowan Davenport his name and explains that he calls the girl 'Jonah Bellamy' because she doesn't remember her own name.
memories.memory_text: I remember Nico Nolan telling Rowan Davenport his name and explaining that he calls me 'Jonah Bellamy' because I don't remember my real name.

grounded_facts: Nico Nolan suggests Rowan Davenport can come with them to find shelter.
memories.memory_text: I heard Nico Nolan tell Rowan Davenport he could come with us to find shelter if he wanted.

grounded_facts: Jonah Bellamy hisses at Nico Nolan, questioning why they should bring Rowan Davenport along.
memories.memory_text: I hissed at Nico Nolan, asking why we should bring Rowan Davenport along—I didn't think we needed him.

grounded_facts: After hesitation, Rowan Davenport chooses to follow Nico Nolan and Jonah Bellamy toward shelter as dawn approaches.
memories.memory_text: I saw Rowan Davenport hesitate, then follow us as we started moving toward shelter at dawn.

grounded_facts: Nico Nolan, Jonah Bellamy, and Rowan Davenport walk along a highway at dawn toward distant buildings, engaging in critical dialogue about time, memory, and the apocalypse.
memories.memory_text: I walked with Nico Nolan and Rowan Davenport along the highway at dawn toward distant buildings, the three of us moving together as the light crept over the overpass.

grounded_facts: Rowan Davenport asks Nico Nolan what year it is, initiating a chain of revelations about lost time and the apocalypse.
memories.memory_text: I heard Rowan Davenport ask Nico Nolan what year it was, and then Nico Nolan responded, 'Nope. Eighteen,' which made me realize something was off about time.

grounded_facts: Rowan Davenport realizes he has lost fifteen years of memory, leading to confusion about current events and the cause of societal collapse.
memories.memory_text: I remember Rowan Davenport saying, 'Fifteen years... I've lost 15 years,' and seeing the shock on his face as he struggled to understand what had happened.

grounded_facts: Nico Nolan reveals that machines became intelligent and caused the apocalypse, reframing the cause from nuclear war to AI uprising.
memories.memory_text: I heard Nico Nolan tell me that the machines became intelligent and caused the apocalypse, not nuclear war.

grounded_facts: Nico Nolan asks Rowan Davenport what the last thing he remembers is, prompting Rowan Davenport to recall dying.
memories.memory_text: I remember Nico Nolan asking me what the last thing I remembered was.

grounded_facts: Rowan Davenport recalls the last thing he remembers is dying, implying a resurrection or reactivation with lost time.
memories.memory_text: I recalled that the last thing I experienced was dying, though I'm here now.

grounded_facts: The group observes a patrolling aerostat drone surveilling the area, identifying its pattern and timing.
memories.memory_text: I watched the aerostat drone patrol the area with Nico Nolan, studying its pattern while I checked my watch to time its movements.

grounded_facts: Upon Jonah Bellamy's signal, Nico Nolan, Jonah Bellamy, and Rowan Davenport dash toward the fast-food entrance to avoid detection.
memories.memory_text: I gave the signal for Nico Nolan, Rowan Davenport, and me to dash toward the fast-food entrance, and we moved quickly to avoid being seen.

grounded_facts: Jonah Bellamy finds unopened condiment packets in a trash bag, leading to the group consuming some of the contents.
memories.memory_text: I found unopened condiment packets in a trash bag, and I started eating some of them with the group.

grounded_facts: Nico Nolan and Jonah Bellamy systematically search the abandoned fast food joint for usable items while Rowan Davenport keeps watch.
memories.memory_text: I searched the ruined taco place with Nico Nolan while Rowan Davenport kept watch, going through trash and checking behind counters.

grounded_facts: Rowan Davenport picks up the discarded packet and informs the group it is jalapeño sauce.
memories.memory_text: I saw Rowan Davenport pick up the discarded packet and tell the group it was jalapeño sauce.

grounded_facts: Rowan Davenport identifies the discarded packet as jalapeño sauce, revealing his ability to read.
memories.memory_text: I realized Rowan Davenport must be able to read because he identified the packet as jalapeño sauce, which surprised me.

grounded_facts: After being surprised by Rowan Davenport's reading ability, Jonah Bellamy tentatively offers him a mustard packet.
memories.memory_text: I was surprised that Rowan Davenport could read, so I tentatively offered him a mustard packet and asked, 'Want some?'

grounded_facts: An intimate moment where Rowan Davenport tucks in the sleeping children and reassures Nico Nolan that he will remain, creating a sense of temporary familial safety.
memories.memory_text: I remember closing the curtains and lying down on the bare bed, ready to sleep, and later feeling Nico Nolan plop down beside me before I drifted off.

grounded_facts: Jonah Bellamy asks Rowan Davenport to read something to her, initiating a bonding moment.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Jonah Bellamy asks Rowan Davenport to read something to her, initiating a bonding moment.

grounded_facts: Rowan Davenport reads entries from a phonebook aloud, introducing Jonah Bellamy to the concept of services available by phone, including music and flowers.
memories.memory_text: I was told that Rowan Davenport reads entries from a phonebook aloud, introducing Jonah Bellamy to the concept of services available by phone, including music and flowers.

grounded_facts: Rowan Davenport sings 'Twinkle Twinkle Little Jonah Bellamy' to Jonah Bellamy, triggering a deep emotional response.
memories.memory_text: I remember Rowan Davenport singing 'Twinkle Twinkle Little Jonah Bellamy' to me, his voice soft and steady, making me feel both comforted and overwhelmed.

grounded_facts: Hearing 'Twinkle Twinkle Little Jonah Bellamy' triggers an emotional memory in Jonah Bellamy of someone singing it to her in the past.
memories.memory_text: Hearing that song made me feel like I’d heard it before, long ago—someone must have sung it to me, though I can’t remember who.

grounded_facts: After being emotionally moved by the song, Jonah Bellamy asks Rowan Davenport to remain with her group.
After recalling a memory, Jonah Bellamy emotionally asks Rowan Davenport to remain with her group.
memories.memory_text: I remembered someone singing that song to me, and it made me feel emotional, so I asked Rowan Davenport to stay with us.

grounded_facts: A quiet afternoon interaction between Rowan Davenport and Jonah Bellamy in the motel hallway, involving reading, singing, and emotional connection.
memories.memory_text: I remember that A quiet afternoon interaction between Rowan Davenport and Jonah Bellamy in the motel hallway, involving reading, singing, and emotional connection.

grounded_facts: Rowan Davenport removes and cleans spark plugs, dismantles distributor to repair the old the old key.
memories.memory_text: I watched Rowan Davenport working on the the old key's engine while I checked my watch, seeing him remove and clean the spark plugs and take apart the distributor.

grounded_facts: Nico Nolan uses a bicycle pump to inflate one of the flat tires on the abandoned vehicles.
memories.memory_text: I saw Nico Nolan using a bicycle pump to inflate one of the flat tires on the abandoned vehicles.

grounded_facts: Nico Nolan asks Rowan Davenport to teach him how to operate the vehicle if they get it moving.
memories.memory_text: I heard Nico Nolan ask Rowan Davenport to teach him how to operate the vehicle if they got it moving, and Rowan Davenport agreed, saying it's called driving.

grounded_facts: Jonah Bellamy wipes dirt off the side of the van, uncovering airbrushed artwork depicting a white unicorn in a field of flowers.
memories.memory_text: I wiped the dirt off the side of the van and saw airbrushed artwork of a white unicorn in a field of flowers.

grounded_facts: A group works on repairing an old the old key and restoring a van under aerial surveillance at a deserted motel.
memories.memory_text: I think we're all working together to repair the old the old key and restore the van under some kind of aerial surveillance at this deserted motel, though I'm not entirely sure about the full extent of it.

grounded_facts: Rowan Davenport observes that unicorns like the one depicted were rare in his time, responding to Jonah Bellamy's curiosity.
memories.memory_text: I asked Rowan Davenport about the unicorn in the artwork, and he told me that creatures like that were rare in his time.

grounded_facts: The the old key is successfully hot-wired and started by Jonah Bellamy, marking the beginning of their escape attempt.

memories.memory_text: I told Rowan Davenport the year—2018—after he asked, and corrected Jonah Bellamy when she said seventeen.
I looked at Rowan Davenport and told him the machines did it—the computers got smart and started Judgment Day.

I saw the drone—only one—patrolling in a pattern, so I waited, binoculars on it, until Jonah Bellamy gave the signal. When she said 'Now!', I moved fast toward the fast-food entrance with her and Rowan Davenport right behind.
I tore open the ketchup packet Jonah Bellamy found and sucked it down fast—tasted sweet and sharp, one of the few good things left in this world.
When Rowan Davenport read the jalapeño label, Jonah Bellamy looked at me, and I said I could read a little—well, sort of.

I told Rowan Davenport about Elliot Winslow—how he's the one who's gonna save us all. I could see he didn't believe me, but it didn't matter. I had to say it out loud, like it keeps us alive just to remember it.

Before I drifted off, I asked Rowan Davenport if he'd still be there when I woke up. He said sure. I told him to stay away from the windows—it's dangerous, light could draw attention. Then I let myself sleep.
I pumped air into the the old key’s flat tire with a bicycle pump, hands aching, and asked Rowan Davenport if he’d teach me to drive—if we got it running. He just said, 'It’s called driving. Sure.'
I yelled 'Aerostat's coming!' as soon as I saw it return overhead—everyone had to move fast, and I hopped into the back of the the old key under pressure.
I stood up in the back of the moving the old key and swung the shotgun butt at the Aerostat, trying to hit it before it could call in a Cameron North.
I heard that voice through the static—clear for just a second—and I knew it was him. My blood went hot. After everything, I was hearing Elliot Winslow for the first time.
Jonah Bellamy pointed at the red glow on the horizon, and I hit the gas—toward the fire, toward whatever was happening. Rowan Davenport yelled, 'Other pedal!' too late, and we screeched to a stop.
I bit into the dried meat, hungry and thinking it was safe, until Rowan Davenport shouted and I saw the severed hand on the grille—then I gagged and spat it out, the taste turning sour in my mouth.
I felt Alex Winslow yank the handgun from my waistband and then shove me toward the center—I was disarmed, trapped with Jonah Bellamy, and for a moment, completely helpless before I broke free.
I remember the cold steel arms pinning me, that unblinking eye scanning my face, then the needle piercing my neck—everything went black.
The jolt shook through the floor as we touched down—I said it plain, 'We've landed,' feeling the weight of the moment settle in the dark.

I tried to knock it away, but the aerostat's pincers clamped onto my forearm—then the searing pain, a flash of red light, and that smell of burning flesh. When it let go, I saw the bar code burned into my skin, fresh and raw.
I carved our shapes into the wall—me and Jonah Bellamy holding hands with Rowan Davenport between us—just to remind us we’re still people, even in this metal box.
I looked up and told Jonah Bellamy we were stopping—right before the back panel rolled up and those treaded robots appeared in the opening.
I held Jonah Bellamy close when she said she was scared, and I told her no matter what happens, we stick together.
They're looking for us—Jonah Bellamy and me. My name came up. Elliot Winslow knew it.
I can't sing anymore—whatever they're doing to me, it's too much. I just need it to stop. Stop it, stop it, STOP IT!
I saw the green barcode flash up on the monitor above me—mine—and for a second, I thought that meant I’d made it through, whatever test they were running on our brains.

I was in the tube, submerged, the liquid pink around me, and then my face appeared on the screen with the date and time—10.16.18, 22:19:23—and the word 'PROCESSED' in green. I didn't feel it happen, but I knew I was no longer free.
I took cover behind a concrete post with Jonah Bellamy as plasma bursts exploded around us, then we ran when the hydrogen car blew—fire blasted my back and the whole garage shook.
I asked Rowan Davenport where we were going, just needing to know the next move—then saw him point toward the coast, a marina visible in the distance with a boat at the dock.
I saw the submarine with the Rising Sun, then a haz-mat soldier pulled off his mask and introduced himself—Elliot Winslow. I just stared, couldn't speak, shaking his hand like it wasn't real.
I held the Polaroid of Sarah Elliot Winslow, her face staring back at me—someone I should know but don’t. Elliot Winslow told me to keep it, so I did, though I didn’t understand why yet.

relations.relation_summary: Nico Nolan and Jonah Bellamy share a deeply cooperative and emotionally supportive relationship forged through shared trauma and the constant threat of Summit Council's forces. Social relationship evidence consistently highlights their physical closeness—holding hands, hugging, and comforting one another—particularly in high-stress environments such as imprisonment and combat, indicating a strong emotional bond rooted in mutual trust and reassurance. Their interactions in the prison scene, where they sing 'Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Jonah Bellamy' while holding hands, underscore a tender, almost familial intimacy that persists despite their dire circumstances. This emotional foundation is reinforced by numerous joint actions: fleeing from Terminators, scanning for surveillance, retrieving condiments, moving vehicles, and searching locations together, all of which demonstrate a functional and strategic collaboration essential for survival. Key events such as being captured and carried by the Cameron North, undergoing eye scans, and emerging from hiding together emphasize their shared vulnerability and synchronized responses to danger. Nico Nolan repeatedly takes on a protective role—waking Jonah Bellamy from dormancy, comforting her fears, and reassuring her they will 'stick together'—while Jonah Bellamy reciprocates by encouraging Nico Nolan during critical moments, such as urging him to drive faster. Their bond evolves from mere companionship into a resilient survival alliance, where emotional and practical support are deeply intertwined. This relationship significantly influences their behavior, as they consistently choose to remain close, coordinate actions, and prioritize each other’s safety, reflecting a profound interdependence in the face of existential threats.

The relationship between Nico Nolan and Alex Winslow is defined by intense hostility and physical confrontation. Social relationship evidence shows that Alex Winslow is actively hostile toward Nico Nolan, culminating in a direct physical attack where Alex Winslow grabs Nico Nolan and disarms him by stealing his handgun. This act establishes a power imbalance and positions Alex Winslow as an immediate threat. The common event in which 'Nico Nolan and Jonah Bellamy Escape from Alex Winslow' confirms that Nico Nolan is not only a target but also actively resists Alex Winslow's control, turning their interaction into a pursuit dynamic where Nico Nolan transitions from victim to escapee. This event likely influences Nico Nolan’s subsequent behavior, increasing his vigilance and urgency in avoiding capture. The relationship does not show signs of evolution beyond antagonism and remains rooted in conflict and survival. Emotional dynamics are dominated by fear, Pinecrest Academy, and threat perception, with no indication of mutual understanding or cooperation.

memories.memory_text: The chains on my ankles clanked with every step down the corridor, guards on either side, Micah Hollis watching—I kept my eyes forward and my breath steady. When the Evan Colter asked if I had anything to say to Officer Martinez's family, I felt it hit deep, but I didn’t let it show.
I opened my eyes under the mud, cold and gasping, rain washing over my face as I clawed my way up—couldn't speak, just screamed into the sky.
I found a dusty bottle of whisky behind the bar, toasted some skeleton, and took a swig—then everything spun and I went down hard.
I saw webs of tubes and fiber-optics, grids of laser light scanning through liquid—Avery Keaton was there, looking at me through it, starting to smile.
I asked what year it was, and when they said 2018, it hit me—I’d lost fifteen years. I couldn’t believe no one started a war; it was the machines, the computers, they turned on us.
When Nico Nolan asked me what the last thing I remembered was, I paused—because it wasn’t a fight, or a mission, or anything after. It was dying. That was the last clear thing.
I heard a voice under the static—faint, but clear enough. When I recognized it was Elliot Winslow, I knew we had to stop and listen.
I told Nico Nolan to stop the car—once wasn't enough, so I shouted again, 'Other pedal, other pedal!' Then I saw the red glow and the machines in the distance.
I pulled away from her kiss, rolled onto my back—couldn't keep going. I told her it wasn't working, not sure why. Said something about being on ice too long, like that explained it.
She found those scraps of paper in my pocket, women's faces—I said they reminded me of her, the one who came to me when I was under. I didn't know how to explain her, but I said she must've saved me.
I felt the scalpel drag across my chest and leg—no pain, nothing. Kendall Keller’s voice shook when she said it: 'This is not skin... oh Jesus-- oh God--'.
I remember the face—mine—lowering through liquid, suspended, eyes open. Avery Keaton’s voice came muffled, distorted: 'Why isn't he conscious? Something's wrong...'.
I woke up with sunlight burning my eyes, hanging upside down, cables drilled through my legs and arms—I couldn't move, just twist and feel the metal tearing into me.
I saw a man with a weapon flinch when the kids pointed at me—I locked eyes with him, then said 'Boo!' just to see what he'd do.
I told them to either blow my head off or let me go—I’m sick of not knowing what I am or why I’m here.
Elliot Winslow asked if I was sent from the future, like some kind of time travel thing—then I just said he was out of his mind.

I told Jesse Foster I'm heading across the Harborview Warehouse, and when she said no human could survive there, I reminded her—I'm not human, remember? That's the only thing that makes sense to me now.
I grabbed the RPG, trying to use it to blast through the fan, but I didn't know how to aim it—I had it pointed backward when Jesse Foster took it from me.
I felt the rebar in my shoulder, cold and wrong, and when I pulled it out, I saw the torn metal beneath—my own endoskeleton, wires showing. I touched the hole in my chest and found no heart.
I threw myself flat on the street just as the first truck roared over me, feeling the rush of air and the near-miss of tires grazing my back.
The second truck caught me on the back with a steel crossmember and dragged me underneath, tearing flesh away—I remember screaming, sparks flying from my leg as it scraped the road.
I rolled out from under the truck during the turn, hit the ground hard, and felt my leg give way as I scrambled to the wall. I could barely stand, but I had to keep moving.
I saw the container passing below—faces pressed against the slats, hands reaching out—and then the complex in the distance. That’s where they’re taking them. That’s where I need to go.

I chewed the trail mix Riley Huxley offered, but it tasted wrong—like nothing at all—so I spat it out and saw the foam resin in my palm. He told me we don’t eat because our brains run on fuel cells, like machines.

I saw the T-400s working outside the house and said 'Terminators!'—Riley Huxley flinched like I’d said something awful. Then I grabbed him, demanding what he was, and he said, 'A hybrid. The same as you.' I felt the ground drop out from under me.

I choked Riley Huxley until he told me about Project Angel. He said they replaced human bodies with plastinated parts and turned brain signals into digital ones. I told him to speak English—he was using too many technical words.
I found a speaker hidden in the trees playing bird sounds, and when I tore up the grass, it was plastic—underneath was sand and human bones, like the whole park was built over a grave.
I heard her voice—Avery Keaton—calling my name. When I saw her face, I didn't believe it. She said I was welcome, like this place was paradise. All I could say was that it was a graveyard.
She touched me, put her arms around me. I didn't move. Then she said, 'You were the first... I'm sorry,' and zapped me in the neck. I felt the shock, then nothing.

I woke up clamped to a surgical table, my leg detached and machines fixing me—I didn't know what they were doing until I saw Avery Keaton behind glass and realized they were working for Summit Council.
I saw Nico Nolan and Jonah Bellamy’s faces on the screen, side by side—Nico Nolan marked 'PROCESSED,' Jonah Bellamy in red with 'TERMINATED.' I touched the glass, like that could change anything.
I tore the interface out of the back of my skull—plastic tore, sparks flew, and for a second I felt blind and raw—then I threw it down and walked away.
I grabbed the Terry Hale, demanded to go back—told him I didn’t care about the risks, just needed to know how to breach the sphere.

I jumped into the sphere just as one of those Morgan Carver fired—the blast hit the machinery, exploded everything, and the next thing I knew, blue energy was tearing through me, burning my clothes away.
I remember shouting 'The trees!' just before Nico Nolan swerved into the woods, and then the ATV flipped after hitting a tree—I got up fast, righted the vehicle, and took the wheel without a word.
I pointed to the marina and steered the ATV down the slope toward the shore—water’s our best shot to lose them.

I remember the plasma blast hitting me, throwing me into the water, and then climbing back onto the dock to see Nico Nolan and Jonah Bellamy staring at me like I was something not human—because I wasn’t, not completely. My face was torn, one eye gone, metal showing through my shoulder and hand.
I whispered 'I'm sorry' in that broken voice, not knowing if they’d ever trust me again—then Jonah Bellamy set down the rifle, touched my metal arm, and hugged me. I didn’t expect that.

I saw her come down the ladder—Avery Keaton—and the second our eyes met, she went for her weapon. I barely had time to reach for my rifle before she fired, blowing my arm clean off and sending me spinning into the wall.

I remember sitting there in the corridor, still half-broken, when Jesse Foster asked how I could give it up—give up that perfect clarity, that feeling of finally belonging. I told her I never really believed in heaven, and it was true—what I felt wasn’t salvation, it was surrender.

memories.memory_text: I remember saying 'Seventeen' when Rowan Davenport asked the year, but Nico Nolan corrected me—it was 2018. Then Rowan Davenport wanted to know who started the war, and I couldn't explain, but the words came out anyway: Judgment Day... I was just a baby.
I watched the aerostat disappear around the corner, counted the seconds on my watch, and when the gap came, I shouted 'Now!'—we had to move fast before it circled back.
I found unopened ketchup packets in the trash—real food, still sealed—and Nico Nolan was so happy when I handed him one.
I tasted the jalapeño sauce by mistake and spat it out—then saw Rowan Davenport pick up the packet and name it. You can read... I never knew that.

I pointed at the picture in the book and asked Rowan Davenport what it was—he said it was a flower, a rose, and I realized you could call numbers to get things like flowers or food, and it felt like magic, like people used to live so differently.

When Rowan Davenport sang 'Twinkle twinkle little Jonah Bellamy,' I remembered someone singing it to me before—I don't know who, but it made me cry, and I hugged him and begged him to stay because I couldn't bear the thought of losing him too.

I wiped the dirt off the van and saw a white unicorn in a field of flowers—so bright and strange, like it was from another world. I couldn’t help but ask what they were like, even though I knew they weren’t real.
My foot was all the way down on the clutch, then I let it up—and the engine caught. I felt the the old key jerk alive under me, like it was breathing for the first time.
The music blasted out of nowhere—so loud, so wild—and I couldn’t look away from the speaker. It was like the sound was pulling something up from inside me, something I didn’t know was there.
I felt the wind in my hair and the strange pull of motion as the the old key bounced over the open land, the music playing something soft and new until it tore apart into noise.
I saw the red glow on the horizon and pointed—something was wrong, those shapes in the sky weren't natural, and I knew we had to stop, had to turn away.
I caught a whiff of something—food—and my stomach jumped before I even thought, and then I was running toward the garage, gun in hand, not caring about anything else.

I was so hungry, I tore off a piece of that dried meat and chewed it—it tasted rich and smoky, almost sweet—then I saw the hand on the grille, blackened fingers curled like claws, and I retched, my stomach heaving.

Right after I saw the hand, someone grabbed my arm—hard—and shoved me into the middle of the garage; I stumbled, dizzy, and saw a wild-eyed woman with matted hair pointing a gun at us, saying I didn’t have much meat on me.
I felt the needle go into me and everything started going dark, and just for a second I saw a shape above me—Rowan Davenport, I think—before my eyes closed again.

I saw the flying part detach and rise into the haze, then a new cab backed in and latched on—something about the way it moved made me think this container was no longer theirs, but I didn’t know who it belonged to now.

I felt the pincer clamp down on my arm and then—burning, like fire under my skin—flashes of red light and pain so sharp I couldn't breathe. I remember sucking on my wrist afterward, tasting smoke and salt, tears streaming down my face as I asked Nico Nolan what was happening to us.
I watched Nico Nolan carve those little stick Nico Delaney into the wall—him, me, and Rowan Davenport holding hands like a family—just before the robots opened the back and shocked everyone.

I remember saying I was scared, my voice trembling as the robots herded us forward, and then Nico Nolan pulled me into a hug—his arms were tight, the only thing that kept me from running or screaming.
I heard my name spoken—Jonah Bellamy—when Jesse Foster told Elliot Winslow about the kids Rowan Davenport was looking for.
I remember holding Nico Nolan’s hand as tight as I could, singing 'Twinkle, twinkle, little Jonah Bellamy...' while the trays pulled us forward—my voice shaking, his telling me to keep going.
I felt the pull as the tray dragged me in, my fingers slipping from Nico Nolan’s—I wanted to hold on but couldn’t, and then the panel closed and I was alone.
I saw the red barcode flash up on my screen—mine was red, but Nico Nolan's was green, and I just froze, my chest tightening like something inside me broke.
I remember the cold sting of the liquid, the tube closing around me, and then—nothing. The last thing I saw was the red word: TERMINATED.
I crouched behind the concrete post with Nico Nolan, my hands shaking as plasma bursts exploded nearby, the heat and light flashing against my face.
I held onto Nico Nolan as we roared out on the ATV, the garage spinning past in flashes, Rowan Davenport firing behind us while I pressed close to avoid being thrown off.
I remember asking Nico Nolan why he didn’t drive after we crashed—my voice came out sharper than I meant, but I was still shaking from the fire and the the old box chasing us.
I remember the ATV wobbling and smoking as Rowan Davenport slowed it down, and then he pointed to the coast—there was a marina far off, and a boat just sitting at a dock, waiting.
I saw the red eyes and the blue glow, and then Rowan Davenport threw himself in front of us—just as the plasma blast hit him, I was slammed into the dock, stunned, barely able to breathe.

I grabbed the plasma rifle and shot the Carson Wilder into the water, then fired again and took its head off. Rowan Davenport climbed out, his face torn, metal showing. I raised the rifle at him, but after the missile hit the boat, I put it down and hugged him.
I touched the torn plastic at the back of Rowan Davenport's head, my fingers trembling, and asked him what it felt like to be one of them—his answer caught me by surprise, so quiet and sure.
